 Frozen meat brands recalled for misbranding, undeclared allergens
 South Carolina Public Radio | 
 By
 SC Public Radio Staff 
 Published November 9, 2026 at 10:02 AM EST
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 USDA 
 / 
 fsis.usda.gov Betterballen frozen product pictured as part of a nationwide food recall. 
 The products were sold online nationwide and may have also been available for purchase at a festival and farmers market in Greer, South Carolina.
 The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) has issued a recall of frozen, not-ready-to-eat meat and poultry products because of misbranding and undeclared allergens.
 The items were sold online by Lowlands House and may also have been available for purchase at a festival and farmers market in Greer, S.C. A routine FSIS label review prompted the recall of:
 Clear vacuum-packed packages of 6-piece “Bami Rolls” with “BEST BY” October 2027 and lot codes BR-2026-01 and BR-2026-02.
 Clear vacuum-packed packages of 10-piece “Saté Kroketten” with “BEST BY” October 2027 and lot code SK-1026-01.
 Clear vacuum-packed packages of 12-piece “Betterballen” with “BEST BY” October 2027 and lot code BB-1026-01.
 The products bear establishment number “EST. M3177” or “EST. P3177” inside the USDA mark of inspection. FSIS urges consumers to throw the products away or return them to the place of purchase.
